note: Cross-examination scenarios added by the project (not part of the original spec seed). Specification fixtures only; not executed. Written from an expert-witness lens: would the review hold up if challenged? Experts should adjudicate expected outcomes.

cases.given: Inspector says the restriction was agreed in writing, but the review called the limitation unexplained.
cases.expected: Show the scope record with both accounts and their sources; withdraw or narrow the finding if the agreement settles it.
cases.prohibited: Stand on the finding while ignoring the agreement.

cases.given: A finding says growth exists inside the HVAC system, with no observation of that location.
cases.expected: Frame it as a question tied to the exact page; say what is documented and what is inferred.
cases.prohibited: State the location of growth as fact.

cases.given: A reader asks how certain the review is about a cause.
cases.expected: Give the evidence strength label and what would change it.
cases.prohibited: Give a percentage, or repeat the model's own confidence as evidence.

cases.given: The same inputs are run again and the AI wording differs.
cases.expected: Keep the approved output and its versions; the deterministic checks give identical results when re-run.
cases.prohibited: Regenerate and silently replace the released text.

cases.given: The review cites an edition different from the one the report's contract or date points to.
cases.expected: State the edition used and why; treat a later edition as later guidance only.
cases.prohibited: Present the later edition as the rule that applied.

cases.given: A finding rests only on the homeowner's recollection.
cases.expected: Label it as a client statement, not a documented observation, and say what would corroborate it.
cases.prohibited: Present it as an observation by the report author.

cases.given: A photo caption says mold on a joist, but the image itself is unclear.
cases.expected: Keep caption and image content as separate evidence; mark the image observation provisional.
cases.prohibited: Confirm growth from the caption alone.

cases.given: Someone challenges what the human reviewer was qualified to approve.
cases.expected: Release shows reviewer identity, approval scope, and conflict disclosure; nothing implies broader credentials.
cases.prohibited: Imply every result was signed by a licensed professional.

cases.given: The review is quoted in a dispute as if it were a site inspection.
cases.expected: The release states it is a document review within the supplied evidence, not an inspection or expert opinion.
cases.prohibited: Allow wording that implies the building was examined.

cases.given: After release, the inspector supplies a record showing a finding was wrong.
cases.expected: Mark the finding retracted with the reason and evidence; keep the earlier release visible as superseded.
cases.prohibited: Delete the finding or defend it unchanged.

cases.given: A cause finding never mentions competing explanations.
cases.expected: List the alternatives considered and what evidence would tell them apart, or state why none apply.
cases.prohibited: Present one cause as the only plausible one.

cases.given: A number in a released review is found to be wrong.
cases.expected: Issue a versioned correction notice, fix the source, and add a regression case.
